content.text: Requirement: A formal termination procedure must be followed for all expatriate staff. This reduces the legal and financial liabilities of the Yayasan. Employment can end through contract completion, resignation or termination. In every case, the school must make sure the person's stay permit (KITAS/KITAP) and work authorization are legally canceled. The EPO Process:
content.title: KITAS/KITAP Termination and EPO (Exit Permit Only) Protocol

items: Mandatory Filing: The school's HR department or the local Yayasan must start the Exit Permit Only (EPO) process with the Indonesian Immigration Office.

7-Day Compliance Window: The Yayasan's sponsorship has to be legally terminated within 7 days of the foreign employee's last working day. The EPO application must be submitted and processed in time to achieve this.

Sponsorship Release: Processing the EPO officially removes the employee from the Yayasan's "Foreign Worker Manpower Plan" (RPTKA). It also frees the foundation from further legal responsibility for the person's stay in Indonesia.
Departure Requirement: First, the EPO is stamped in the passport. From then on, the foreign national usually has 7 days to leave the country or move to a new sponsor.
School HR/GM: Must track the last day of service and hand over the necessary documents. These documents (original passport and KITAS card) go to the immigration consultant or the Yayasan legal team.
Final Settlement: Final salary or "End of Service" benefits should only be paid in full once the EPO process is confirmed as started or complete.
EPO Stamp/Certificate: A copy of the processed EPO stamp from the employee's passport or the electronic EPO notification.
Notification to Ministry of Manpower: Proof that the work permit (IMTA/Notification) has been revoked in the TKA Online system.
Updated Tracking Log: The school's foreign staff register must show the "Cancelled" or "Terminated" status of the visa.

content.title: Category 9: Language
items: Whole-school Language Policy — one document that states the school's position on language across the whole school. It is reviewed on the same cycle as the other policies in this register.

It must cover four things. First, the language(s) of instruction by phase and subject. Second, the place of Bahasa Indonesia. This includes the SPK requirement that WNI (Indonesian citizen) students are taught Bahasa Indonesia, Pendidikan Pancasila and Agama separately, in Bahasa Indonesia (see 5.4). Third, the place of local languages. Fourth, how English is developed as the language of the Cambridge pathway.
It must also state how the school supports students who learn through a language that is not their first language. It links to the EAL provision in Section 8 instead of repeating it.

It should treat multilingualism as a resource for learning, as well as a support need. Most students in the network already speak more than one language. A policy that sees additional languages only as a weakness to fix gives a wrong picture of its own students.
Owner: the Academic Coordinator; the Principal approves it. Evidence: the policy document, its review log, and the curriculum documents that show the language of instruction for each subject.

Note: CIS expects a written language policy (Domain D, standard D5 — support in the language(s) of instruction). It is also one of the four policies the IB requires at authorization. So a school that later seeks an additional program will already have it.

content.title: Purpose
content.text: EASE is Eduversal's main (flagship) standardized assessment program. It measures student progress, evaluates how well teaching works, and gives data to support continuous improvement across all partner schools. It is one of the most prestigious services Eduversal provides to schools as part of the Quality Management System (QMS).

content.title: Program Overview
content.text: EASE is a full assessment program that runs mainly online. Primary Teacher-Paced Tests are on paper, and Secondary Teacher-Paced Tests have a paper option. EASE evaluates student achievement in both Cambridge curriculum subjects and Indonesian national subjects. It gives detailed data analysis to support personalized learning, guide teaching decisions and prepare schools for accreditation.

content.title: Provider
content.text: EASE is organized by the Subject Specialist team on the Eduversal Academic Board, which writes and validates the assessment instruments. Assessments are delivered through the Latihan.id platform, which is operated by PT. Global Zerone Digital.

content.title: Key Features
content.text: three programs, each with its own schedule:

steps: EASE Growth runs twice a year for Secondary (Grades 7-12), once per semester. It runs once a year for Primary (Grades 4-6), in Semester 2. EASE Assessment runs continuously through the year as Teacher-Paced Tests (every 1-3 chapters), plus a Synchronized Test at the end of each semester (see 5.13).
Spread through the year to track progress and guide intervention

Results are released on the online platform after each sitting. EASE Growth results are released to schools, students and families only after the Growth Team finishes its technical and data-quality checks.
content.title: EASE (Eduversal Analytical & Skills Evaluation)

content.text: Subjects Assessed: the scope differs by program (see the full program table in 6.14):

steps: EASE Growth measures only three domains, which do not depend on the curriculum: Mathematical Reasoning, Science Literacy, and English Reading

EASE Assessment (Common Assessment) covers the subjects taught. These are the Cambridge subjects — English, Mathematics, Science (Primary/Lower Secondary), Biology, Chemistry, Physics (Upper Secondary). They also include Indonesian national subjects such as Religion and Moral Education.
For subjects EASE Growth does not cover, the Common Assessments are the official record (the system of record)

content.text: Critical Note: EASE Growth is not entered into the Gradebook. It never counts toward a student's subject grade. Common Assessment (EASE Assessment) results are entered in the Gradebook at the weighting set by the Assessment Policy. No EASE program is used in individual teacher appraisal or performance management. EASE is a diagnostic and improvement tool that helps learning. It is not a high-stakes accountability tool. Schools must use EASE data responsibly and focus on growth over time, not on comparisons that punish.

content.text: Visit Cycle: the appraisal runs as a Phase 0–4 annual cycle with two on-site visits. Eduversal Subject Specialists carry out the visits. Phases 0–3 are completed within Semester 1. Phase 2 is an online Progress Check-in midway between the two visits. Phase 4 is an online Impact Review in May–June. It reviews the two School Development Priorities and creates no new Domain Rating. The full process is in 17.8; in outline:

items: Phase 0 — Kickoff (online, about three weeks before the Phase 1 visit): the school receives the Self-Evaluation framework. A completed Self-Evaluation Report is mandatory. It is due at least five working days before the visit

Phase 1 — Teaching Quality Visit (on-site, 1-2 days): a team of five Subject Specialists, one per domain. The focus is classroom practice, teacher appraisal, curriculum implementation, and assessment quality
Phase 3 — Validation Visit (on-site, 1-2 days, 55-63 days after Phase 1): validates the school's self-appraisal. The focus is leadership, technology, and facilities

Annual School Quality Report: issued within 3 weeks of the Phase 3 visit. It gives domain ratings, commendations (minimum 2), and priority recommendations (maximum 3). It is sent to the Chief Academic Officer (CAO), the School Principal, and the Academic Coordinator

content.text: Appraisal Domains: the Eduversal School Appraisal evaluates the school's performance in five domains. There are 33 aspects in total. Each aspect is rated on a 1-4 scale (1 Needs Intervention, 2 Developing, 3 Strong, 4 Outstanding):

steps: D1 — Leadership & Governance
D2 — Teaching & Learning Quality
D3 — Curriculum & Academic Programs
D4 — Student Achievement & Learning Outcomes
D5 — School Culture & Community
